metadata.case_name: HO YUK YIN AND OTHERS v. LAU AH LUNG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: her right foot was severely degloved exposing the underlying tendon and bone;
source: her right foot was severely degloved exposing the underlying tendon and bone;
injuries.icd_description: Other specified open wound of ankle or foot

injuries.description: the distal phalanx of the right big toe was fractured;
source: the distal phalanx of the right big toe was fractured;

injuries.description: there were also fractures of the 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bones.
source: there were also fractures of the 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bones.

injuries.description: During treatment she has undergone two major operations. The first operation, immediately after the accident, involved debridement and open amputation of all toes of the right foot, a free neurovascular myocutaneous flap operation was performed to cover the main raw area of the right foot followed by a split thickness skin graft operation. More recently, on 17th July 1985, a further revision amputation operation was carried out to improve the skin cover over the stump of the right foot.
source: During treatment she has undergone two major operations. manifestations.description: she was unable to walk for more than 10 or 15 minutes without pain.
she feels pain if she walks any considerable distance
her ability to participate in sports has been substantially reduced.
she only takes part in limited warming up physical education exercises and is unable to attend Junior Police Club camps and other physical activities.
The present limp will remain permanent.

The stump is ugly. The scarring is surprisingly extensive. I appreciate that by another two years the keloids should resolve leaving flat scars but some of this remaining scarring will be visible if she wears dresses.
substantial scarring of her leg and thighs in the donor areas for the skin grafts.
permanent disability of her right foot together with substantial scarring of her leg and thighs in the donor areas.

treatments_received: open amputation of all toes of the right foot
free neurovascular myocutaneous flap operation to cover the main raw area of the right foot
skin taken from the right and left thighs for the skin graft operations

losses.description: Permanent disability of her right foot; the amputation of part of her right foot represents 70% impairment of the foot and 21% impairment of the whole person.
Permanent cosmetic damage: the stump is ugly and scarring is surprisingly extensive; some scarring will be visible if she wears dresses; unlikely ever to be able to wear fashion shoes.
Substantial scarring of her leg and thighs in the donor areas for the skin grafts.
Deprived of a vital part of the spring in walking and stability of the foot in weight-bearing; unable to walk more than short periods without pain; present limp will remain permanent.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Ability to participate in sports substantially reduced; unable to attend Junior Police Club camps and other physical activities; only takes part in limited warming up physical education exercises.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Interruption to her schooling caused her to repeat Primary 4.
